title: Prefix Tree
statement:
Implement a prefix tree (trie) that stores lowercase words.

Contract
- `insert(word)` stores a word. Inserting the same word again changes nothing.
- `contains(word)` is true only if exactly that word was inserted earlier. A word that is merely the start of an inserted word is not contained.
- `hasPrefix(prefix)` is true if at least one inserted word starts with `prefix`; a full inserted word counts as a prefix of itself.
- Words and prefixes are non-null, non-empty, and use only the letters `a` to `z`.

Examples
- After `insert("apple")`: `contains("apple")` is true, `contains("app")` is false, and `hasPrefix("app")` is true.
- After `insert("car")` and `insert("cart")`: `contains("car")` and `contains("cart")` are true, `contains("carts")` is false.
- A new tree contains nothing: `contains("a")` and `hasPrefix("a")` are false.

examples.input: insert apple; contains apple, contains app, hasPrefix app
insert car, insert cart; contains car, contains cart, contains carts
new tree; contains a, hasPrefix a

hints: Each node represents one letter; the path from the root spells a prefix. Store the children of a node by letter.
A node needs a flag saying that an inserted word ends there, so that `contains` can tell a stored word from a mere prefix.

`contains` and `hasPrefix` walk one node per letter and differ only in the final check. Intended complexity: O(L) time per operation for a word of length L, and O(n) space overall when n is the total number of letters stored.
inputSyntax: Input: operations separated by commas, for example: insert apple, contains app, hasPrefix app, contains apple
sampleInput: insert apple, contains app, hasPrefix app, contains apple
